title: Postmortem Quality Gate and Peer Review Workflow
author: Aisha Chen
content:
Summary:
This page defines the Postmortem Quality Gate and Peer Review Workflow for all incidents that impact Redwood Inference production services. It codifies acceptance criteria for postmortems, an evidence-pack checklist, reviewer responsibilities, and automated signals that route postmortems for escalation (legal/compliance/exec). The goal is faster learning cycles, consistent artifacts for audits, and clearer action item ownership.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all incidents classified severity P0, P1, and any P2 that meets the "impactful" criteria below.
- Excludes routine maintenance items documented in a maintenance note; maintenance exceptions must be flagged and routed through the Incident Commander.

Impactful criteria (triggers this workflow):
1) Customer-facing SLO breach: Monthly availability < 99.5% for a customer tenant or any single-region outage > 1 hour.
2) Latency SLO regression: p95 generation latency increase > 2x baseline for > 30 minutes.
3) Data integrity event: confirmed data loss, leak, or material misrouting (any scope).
4) Regulatory or contractual exposure: incident with potential PII or contractual SLA credit implications.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Primary Responder: collects logs, timelines, and initial evidence pack (owner through 48h).
- Incident Commander (IC): validates severity classification, assigns Postmortem Owner within 24 hours.
- Postmortem Owner: produces draft postmortem, files action items, and coordinates reviewers.
- Reviewers (2 required): at least one cross-functional (SRE/platform/product) and one domain expert.
- Executive reviewer: required when incident meets regulatory/enterprise customer thresholds.

Timelines (hard SLAs for artifacts):
- 48 hours: initial postmortem draft uploaded to Confluence with an evidence pack link.
- 7 days: peer review completed and postmortem accepted or routed for rewrite.
- 14 days: all action items owned and triaged; critical actions (P0/P1) should have ETA within 7 days.

Peer Review acceptance criteria (Quality Gate):
The reviewer must mark PASS on all items below for the postmortem to be accepted. If any item is FAIL, the postmortem is returned for revision with reviewer comments.
- Clear problem statement: concise description of failure and boundary (service(s), region, tenant(s)).
- Chronological timeline: events recorded in chronological order with timestamps (UTC) and causal links.
- Evidence pack attached: contains logs, traces, runbook excerpts, and config diffs (see Evidence Pack checklist).
- Root cause analysis (RCA): clearly documented root cause(s) and mitigating factors; avoid speculation beyond available evidence.
- Action items: specific, owner-assigned, with severity and ETA. No more than 10 outstanding P0/P1 actions without exec visibility.
- Customer impact quantified: affected tenants, requests lost, SLA credit estimate (if applicable).
- Lessons learned: concrete changes to runbooks, alerts, or product behavior.
- Postmortem tone: factual, blameless, and constructive.

Evidence Pack checklist (table representation):
| Item | Required | Example source |
|------|----------|----------------|
| Timeline export (span logs/traces) | required | Honeycomb/Grafana trace link |
| Token-level cost/latency slice | required | Redwood Console route view export |
| Error/log snapshots with request IDs | required | ELK: error-2026-02-09.log snippet |
| Configuration diffs around deploy/event | required | Git commit/PR links |
| Infrastructure events (scaler/autoscale/instance health) | required | CloudWatch/Stackdriver alerts |
| Runbook excerpt used | recommended | runbooks/runbook-id-serve-kv-eviction.md |
| Customer complaint transcripts (redacted) | recommended when customer-facing | Support ticket links (Zendesk) |
| Screenshots of status page / customer notices | recommended | Status page archive link |
| Forensic artifacts (HSM/KMS access logs) | required for data-security incidents | KMS audit export |

Postmortem template (constrained outline):
1. Title: <service> outage — YYYY-MM-DD UTC
2. Summary (1–3 sentences)
3. Severity classification and why
4. Impact (tenants, duration, lost requests, SLA exposure)
5. Timeline (bullet list with timestamps)
6. Detection and mitigation steps taken during the incident
7. Root cause analysis (evidence-backed)
8. Post-incident mitigations applied during incident
9. Action items (owner, severity, ETA)
10. Follow-up and monitoring plan
11. Attachments / evidence pack links

Reviewer workflow (step-by-step):
1) Postmortem Owner creates draft in the oncall-and-incident-response space and sets label = "pm-draft".
2) Owner assigns two reviewers and @mentions them in the page.
3) Automated bot (postmortem-bot) checks for the evidence pack link; if missing after 24h it moves the page to status = "in_review" and notifies IC.
4) Reviewers add inline comments and then leave a top-level decision comment: PASS / MINOR_REVISION / MAJOR_REVISION / ESCALATE.
5) MINOR_REVISION: Owner addresses comments and re-requests review; 72h re-review SLA.
6) MAJOR_REVISION: if root-cause or evidence is incomplete, reviewers may escalate to the IC for a rewrite.
7) ESCALATE: triggers exec/legal review if regulatory or enterprise impact criteria met.

Automated signals and gating rules:
- If more than 3 reviewers tag "evidence_missing", the system locks acceptance and triggers a forensic evidence task assigned to the Primary Responder.
- If incident triggered an SLA credit (automatic flag from billing pipeline), the postmortem is CC'd to finance-legal and the exec reviewer.
- If action items include code changes planned to address the RCA, a linked PR must reference the postmortem page ID before closure.

Severity classification guidance (quick table):
| Severity | Definition | Required reviewers |
|----------|------------|--------------------|
| P0 | Complete outage for >=1 region or multi-tenant service down | 3 reviewers + exec review |
| P1 | Partial service loss, high-error-rate impacting many customers | 2 reviewers |
| P2 (impactful) | Single-tenant outage or minor regression meeting triggers above | 2 reviewers (cross-functional recommended) |

Escalation paths for blocked reviews:
- If reviewers do not complete within 7 days, IC escalates to team lead and posts an update in #incident-ops.
- If evidence is contested (conflicting logs/traces), open a Forensics ticket and tag security-forensics@redwood.com.

Templates: top-level reviewer decision comment (copy/paste):
"REVIEW DECISION: [PASS | MINOR_REVISION | MAJOR_REVISION | ESCALATE]
Summary of concerns (if any): <bullet list>
Required next steps: <bullet list>
Reviewer name: <name>
Decision date (UTC): <YYYY-MM-DD>"

Automated Confluence labels and lifecycle states (for search and audits):
- pm-draft: initial draft state; not discoverable in audit exports.
- pm-under-review: reviewers assigned.
- pm-accepted: passed quality gate.
- pm-escalated: legal/exec flagged.
- pm-archived: retained in archive after action items closed.

Auditing and evidentiary retention:
- Accepted postmortems will be exported monthly to our archival bucket with metadata (owner, reviewers, severity) for 7 years for regulatory purposes.
- For incidents with data-security exposure, evidence must be retained immutable for 10 years and access audited via KMS.

Game-day integration and training:
- Every quarter the oncall training program will sample 2 accepted postmortems and run a 90-minute blameless review session in Game Day.
- Postmortem Owner is expected to present the postmortem in the next scheduled Game Day or delegate to the IC.

KPIs and metrics for the program (tracked in Redwood Console):
- Time to first draft (target <= 48h)
- Time to acceptance (target <= 7 days)
- % accepted on first review (target >= 60%)
- Action item closure rate at 30 days (target >= 80%)

Related runbooks and pages:
- Incident evidence chain and forensic runbook (link above)
- Incident comm and postmortem framework (link above)
- Runbook: runbooks/serving-runtime-rollback.md

Appendix A: Example short postmortem decision log entry (for status page archive):
- 2026-02-09T15:24Z | Postmortem created by @aisha.chen.
- 2026-02-10T09:02Z | Reviewer Marco Ruiz: MINOR_REVISION (missing config diff).
- 2026-02-12T10:45Z | Postmortem accepted.

Appendix B: Frequently asked questions:
Q: Who signs off an action item closure for P0?
A: The IC or designated tech lead must add a closure comment referencing the PR/monitoring proof and @mention the Postmortem Owner.

Q: What if customers request the full evidence pack?
A: Provide a redacted summary; escalate to legal for any full-forensic disclosure. Use confidentiality = restricted for those pages and CC account security.
